- Mezcla de todos
  - Kadmos, hijo de Agenor y Argiope, Reyes Tebanos, por noble designio se ganó a la sabia Harmonía, la Obediente a Zeus, quien unida por el cinturon que guia el deseo nupcial, llevó en su vientre la semilla de muchos hijos que trajo al mundo uno por uno, Autonoe, Ino, Agave, Polydoros y por ultimo Semele. Esta ultima, la cuarta de las hijas, creció siendo imagen de las Gracias en su encantadora belleza, preservada para Zeus
- Pindaro
  - "Kadmos (Cadmus) by high design won sage Harmonia, as his wedded wife, who obeyed the voice of Zeus, and became the mother of Semele famed among men."
- Apollodorus
  - "Kadmos (Cadmus) had as daughters [by Harmonia] Autonoe, Ino, Semele, and Agaue (Agave), and one son Polydoros."
- Pausanias
  - "Kadmos (Cadmus) made a brilliant marriage, if, as the Greek legend says, he indeed took to wife [Harmonia] a daughter of Aphrodite and Ares. His daughters too have made him a name; Semele was famed for having a child by Zeus"
- Siculus
  - "Marrying Harmonia, daughter of Aphrodite, he [Kadmos (Cadmus)] begat by her Semele."
- Hyginus
  - "Cadmus, son of Agenor and Argiope, by Harmonia, daughter of Mars [Ares] and Venus [Aphrodite], begat four daughters--Semele, Ino, Agave, Autonoe--and a son, Polydorus."
- Nonnus
  - "Soon Harmonia yoked by the cestus-girdle that guides wedded desire, carried in her womb the seed of many children whom she brought forth soon one by one: turn by turn she was delivered of her teeming burden by the birth of daughters, after four times nine circuits had been fulfilled . . . Then Semele fourth of the daughters grew up, the image of the Kharites (Charites, Graces) in her lovestriking looks, preserved for Zeus; although youngest of the sisters, she alone was given by nature the prerogative of unconquerable beauty."

- Re-escrito
  - Este es el origen de Sémele la madre de Dionisio:
  - Su padre era Kadmos, Rey Tebano, de linaje fenicio, hijo del Rey de Tiro Ágenor y su esposa Argíope. Su madre, la Sabia Harmonía, la Obediente a Zeus, quienes juntos procrearon 5 hijos: Inó, Autónoe, Ágave, Polidóros y por ultimo Sémele.
  - Esta ultima, la cuarta de las hijas, creció siendo imagen de las Járites por su encantadora belleza, que estaba ya escrita, preservada para Zeus
  - Sémele la de bello rostro y cubierta de blanco, se unió en amor con el Dios Electrico y Todo Poderoso, pues quedó enamorado cuando lo invocó ella misma. Bajando ante ella para compartir lecho desde ese dia, en su Palacio de la  Polis Tebana la vistaba por las noches disfrazado de mortal, y sin decir una palabra.
  - Tiempo atras habia soñado esta doncella con  una planta que se quemaba, pero quedando sus frutos intactos, asi que despues de contarle a su padre del misterioso sueño, acuden con el famoso profeta ciego Tiresias quien les indica calmar a Zeus con una ofrenda taurina, sacrificada con sus propias manos. Despues de terminar el rito, se va a bañar al rio Asopos pues quedo empapada de sangre. Zeus observandola de lejos quedó maravillado por lo que se transforma en aguila para acercarse, y poder hablar con ella, y siguendola desde ese dia.
  - Zeus habia tenido un hijo ya, Zagreus el "divino cazador", del amor de Perséfone, pero había sido desmembrado por los Titanes, y él guardando su corazón, se lo dio de beber a Sémele para que renaciera en el fruto de su vientre. Por eso se le llamaba a Dionisio "Dimétor" el de las dos madres, pues Perséfone fue la primera, y después renacido dentro de Semele. ((⏱️=800))
  - Ya embarazada, esperando un esplendido hijo inmortal, Hera se entera, y trata de ganarse su confianza para engañarla transformada en una nana de la Corte Cadmia, Béroe, con su pelo blanco y piel frágil, para que asi le contara con todo lujo de detalles como estaba la situación:
  - "Pero estas segura que es el mismisimo Zeus? no sea que te este engañando un muchacho del pueblo pequeña, que quiera ganarse tu favor para sus propios fines...  mira, la proxima vez que lo veas preguntale si puede llegar contigo en su forma divina, tal cual se acuesta con Hera, para que te despejes de toda duda y disfrutes la verdadera gloria de un Dios"
  - Semele, al siguiente dia que se encuentra con Zeus, le pide que le cumpla un deseo suyo, a lo que Zeus responde que lo que ella pidiese se le concedería, jurandolo por el poder del temible Rio Estigia del Orden Cosmico.
  - Ella, demasiado exitosa, feliz en su ruina, condenada por la generosidad de su amante, respondió "la proxima vez que vengas a mi, muestrate tal cual eres, como cuando te sostiene en su pecho Hera en el abrazo del amor.’
  - Zeus habia sellado sus labios, sin mas remedio que cumplirlo llegando a su camara nupcial en un carruaje electrico y fulgurante, en una forma incandescente.
  - Semele incapaz de presenciar su electrica divinidad en persona arrojó al bebe en lo que fuera un parto prematuro y murio quemada, consumida por su regalo de amor.
  - Zeus tomó al abortado seismesino en sus brazos y lo cosió dentro de su muslo, para que se terminara de gestar, que al nacer fue el agraciado Dionisio, el Hijo engendrado por Zeus.
  - Despues del funeral circulo el rumor entre sus hermanas que habia dormido con una persona del pueblo y que habia acusado a Zeus de ser el padre del niño y por ese karma le llegó la muerte por un rayo.
  - Quien cuido al niño?
    - (version a) al nacer le dio el niño a Hermes para que lo cuidara, y lo llevó al Monte Nysa donde las ninfas del lugar lo nutrieron y criaron.
    - (version b) los habitantes de Brasiai (las Arrojadas) de Laconia tienen otra version en la que despues de morir Semele, Zeus se lleva su cuerpo en un cofre junto con el bebe, que siendo arrastrado por las olas hasta esta region, fue encontrado por los oriundos de esas tierras, dandole un propio funeral a la mujer y criando al niño.
    - los habitantes de Brasiai añaden que Ino la hermana de Semele, llegó a la region y acepto convertirse en la nodriza de Dionisio. Ellos muestran la cuerva donde Ino lo amamantó y llaman al llano el Jardin de Dionisio
    - (version c)

  - (version c)

  - Dionisio trajo a su madre desde el Reino del Hades, con permiso de las Moiras y de su Padre, bajando desde el Lago Alkyonia en Lerna, tal como le explicó el pastor Prosymnos que lo amaba. Despues que la trajo al mundo mortal, bañandose despues su nuevo cuerpo en fuego purificador para recibir la inmortalidad, despue la escoltó hasta el Monte Olimpo, donde la esperaban los Dioses con el nombre de Thyone "la Sacrificada"

Semele la de los rizos ondeantes se quedó a vivir entre los inmortales, despues del rugido electrico, y Pallas siempre la ama, y Zeus no menos, y con mucho cariño su hijo el Viñero Dionisio

- Theogonia de Hesiodo
  - "And Semele, daughter of Kadmos (Cadmus) was joined with him in love [with Zeus] and bare him a splendid son, joyous Dionysos,--a mortal woman an immortal son. And now they both are gods."
- Himno Homerico 1 Dionisiaco
  - "By the deep-eddying river Alpheios (Alpheus) that pregant Semele bare you [Dionysos] to Zeus the thunder-lover. And others yet, lord, say you were born in Thebes: but all of these lie."
- Himno Homerico 7 Dionisiaco
  - "Dionysos, the son of glorious Semele . . . Child of fair-faced Semele."
- Himno Homerico 26 Dionisiaco
  - "[Dionysos] splendid son of Zeus and glorious Semele."
- Oda Pitia 3 de Pindaro
  - "To one [of the daughters of Kadmos (Cadmus) and Harmonia], Thyone the white-armed maiden, Zeus the almighty father came down to her to share her lovely bed."
- Oda de Pindaro (Semele la de larga Cabellera)
  - zōei en Olympiois = vive entre los Olimpicos
  - apothanoisa bromo keraunw = la asesinada por el fulgor de un rayo
  - tanyeithera Semela = Semele la del cabello largo
  - philei de nin Pallas aiei kai Zeus Pater mala  = Atenea siempre la ama, y Zeus mas
  - philei de pais o kissophoros = y ama a su hijo el coronado con hiedra
  - ἀτὰρ λευκολένω γε Ζεὺς πατήρ  ἦλυθεν ἐς λέχος ἱμερτὸν Θυώνα. = pero Padre Zeus llevo al deseado lecho a la de codos blancos, la Sacrificada
  - kadmou korai, semela men olympiadwn agyiatis = Hijas de Cadmo, tu Semele guiadora de los Olimpios
  - Semelan helikampyka = Semele la coronada con diadema
- Bacchylides fr19
  - "Kadmos (Cadmus), who in seven-gated thebes fathered Semele; and she gave birth to Dionysos."
- Ps-Apolodoro, Bibliotheca 3.26
  - "Zeus fell in love with Semele and slept with her, promising her anything she wanted, and keeping it all from Hera. But Semele was deceived by Hera into asking her to come to her as he came to Hera during their courtship. So Zeus, unable to refuse her, arrived in her bridal chamber in a chariot with lightning flashes and thunder, and sent a thunderbolt at her. Semele died of fright, and Zeus grabbed from the fire her sixth-month aborted baby, which he sewed into his thigh. After Semele's death the remaining daughters of Kadmos (Cadmus) circulated the story that she had slept with a mortal, thereafter accusing Zeus, and because of this had been killed by a thunderbolt."
- Ps-Apolodoro Bibliotheca 3.31
  - "[Aktaion (Actaeon)] was later eaten up on Kithairon (Cithaeron) by this own dogs. Acccording to Acousilaos (Acusilaus) [Greek mythographer C6th B.C.], he met his end in this manner because he enraged Zeus by courting Semele."
- Ps-Apolodoro, Bibliotheca 3.38
  - "He [Dionysos] retrieved his mother [Semele] from Haides' realm, gave her the name Thyone, and escorted her up to the sky."
- Siculus, Historia 4.2.1
  - "Semele was loved by Zeus because of her beauty, but since he had his intercourse with her secretly and without speech she thought that the god despised her; consequently she made the request of him that he come to her embraces in the same manner as in his approaches to Hera. Accordingly, Zeus visited her in a way befitting a god, accompanied by thundering and lightning, revealing himself to her as he embraced her; but Semele, who was pregnant and unable to endure the majesty of the divine presence, brought forth the babe untimely and was herself slain by the fire. Thereupon Zeus, taking up the child [Dionysos], handed it over to the care of Hermes, and ordered him to take it to the cave in Nysa . . . where he should deliver it to the Nymphai (Nymphs)."
- Siculus Historia 5.52.1
  - "Zeus, on the occasion when Semele had been slain by his lightning before the time for bearing the child, took the babe and sewed it up in his thigh."
- Siculus, Historia 4.25.4
  - "The myths relate that Dionysos brought up his mother Semele from Hades, and that, sharing with her his own immortality, he changed her name to Thyone."
- Pausanias, Descripcion de Grecia 3.24.4
  - "The inhabitants [of Brasiai (Brasiae) in Lakedaimonia] have a story, found nowhere else in Greece, that Semele, after giving birth to her son by Zeus, was discovered by Kadmos (Cadmus) and put with Dionysos into a chest, which was washed up by the waves in their country. Semele, who was no longer alive when found, received a splendid funeral, but they brought up Dionysos. For this reason the name of their city, hitherto Oreiatai, was changed to Brasiai after the washing up of the chest to land . . . The people of Brasiai add that Ino in the course of her wanderings came to the country and agreed to become the nurse of Dionysos. They show the cave where Ino nursed him, and call the plain the garden of Dionysos."
- Pausanias, Descripcion de Grecia 2.31.2
  - "[In the temple of Artemis at Troizenos (Troezen) in Argolis :] are altars to the gods said to rule under the earth. It is here that they say Semele was brought out of Haides by Dionysos, and that Herakles dragged up the Hound of Haides. But I cannot bring myself to believe even that Semele died at all, seeing that she was the wife of Zeus."
- Pausanias, Descripcion de Grecia 2.37.6
- Philostratos, Imagines 1.14
  - "[Ostensibly a description of an ancient Greek painting in Neapolis (Naples) :] Bronte (Thunder), stern of face, and Astrape (Lightning) flashing light from her eyes, and raging fire from heaven that has laid hold of a king's house, suggest the following tale, if it is one you know. A cloud of fire encompassing Thebes breaks into the dwelling of Kadmos (Cadmus) as Zeus comes wooing Semele; and Semele apparently is destroyed, but Dionysos is born, by Zeus, so I believe, in the presence of the fire. And the form of Semele is dimly seen as she goes to the heavens, where the Mousai (Muses) will hymn her praises : but Dionysos leaps forth as his mother's womb is rent apart and he makes the flame look dim, so brilliantly does he shine like a radiant star."
- Hyginus, Fabular 155
  - "Sons of Jove [Zeus] . . . Liber [Dionysos] by Semele daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia."
- Hyginus, Fabulae 167
  - "Liber [Dionysos-Zagreus], son of Jove [Zeus] and Proserpina [Persephone], was dismembered by the Titanes (Titans), and Jove [Zeus] gave his heart, torn to bits, to Semele in a drink. When she was made pregnant by this, Juno [Hera], changing herself to look like Semele's nurse, Beroe, said to her : ‘Daughter, ask Jove [Zeus] to come to you as he comes to Juno, so you may know what pleasure it is to sleep with a god.’ At her suggestion Semele made this request of Jove, and was smitten by a thunderbolt. He took Liber [Dionysos] from her womb, and gave him to Nysus to be cared for. For this reason he is called Dionysus, and also ‘the one with two mothers.’"
- Hyginus, Fabular 179
  - "Jove [Zeus] desired to lie with Semele, and when Juno [Hera] found out, she changed her form to that of the nurse Beroe, came to Semele, and suggested that she ask Jove to come to her as he came to Juno, ‘that you may know,’ she said, ‘what pleasure it is to lie with a god.’ And so Semele asked Jove [Zeus] to come to her in this way. Her request was granted, and Jove, coming with lightning and thunder, burned Semele to death. From her womb Liber [Dionysos] was born.
